primitives.breakdown_regime: When token bucket depletes before refill, client enters backoff phase.

reasoning_traces.think:
The ATB algorithm operates by modeling each client’s access to a shared rate-limited resource through a stochastic token bucket. When a client receives an HTTP 429, it reduces its token refill rate, effectively slowing down its request pace. This process is repeated iteratively until the system stabilizes at a fair share of the global quota. The mathematical formulation involves a differential equation describing token accumulation and depletion, with feedback control adjusting the refill rate based on 429 signals. In GSE, this translates to a dynamic retry policy where each fetch script adjusts its timing based on past throttling events. The dual nature of ATB lies in its ability to act both as a rate limiter and a learning mechanism—its performance improves with more data. Failure modes include oscillation around optimal rates due to delayed feedback or excessive adaptation, leading to suboptimal throughput or increased latency.
